That is the first real movement on the Green bar's "documented" half, which had not started as of 9/17. Next step named by Anne: the package needs review by Brian and Mike before it goes further — which also answers Albert's open SCB question (the async agree/disagree review is still wanted, NOT overtaken by events; the goal reached green on 9/16 via Cameron's bar rewrite, not because the packaging shipped). New Green bar drops the Rippling-app requirement (the Monday intake form now counts) and moves the date to EOQ; Super Green adds a manager-specific WC training session (alongside the mover one) and an FMLA cross-reference on the real leave case. Status moves yellow → green against the new bar. First real engagement with this goal all quarter (8/26). Anne's problem statement: injuries currently surface after the fact via the WC carrier, not proactively; a 3-day gray period where movers self-manage soreness-vs-injury at home produces zero visibility; branch managers are being migrated out of the reporting/admin chain in favor of EE owning it directly. Recommendations discussed, none decided or built yet: (1) decouple 'report the incident' (mandatory, same-day, no-penalty) from 'is it a real injury' (assessed after); (2) two structured EE touchpoints during the gray period instead of silence; (3) split who physically responds on-site (still BM/lead — unavoidable) from who owns the paperwork (fully EE); (4) a 24/7 nurse triage line (Concentra, already used for the HPE) to solve after-hours clinic-or-not calls by phone instead of a manager driving to a job site; (5) automate the old paper-packet idea as an auto-sent one-pager the moment an incident is reported; (6) sequence tooling light-to-heavy — Monday form or text line first to prove the reporting-behavior change, custom app only after that's proven. 8/31: Anne's written recommendation done, socializing with Brian + Mike. 9/3: first real design session with Brian landed a concrete two-track model — serious injuries (medical intervention needed) trigger an incident report → WC process immediately; minor injuries/close calls get a firm 3-day off-schedule window with a mandatory day-3 check-in that forces a doctor visit if unresolved (generalizes the same 3-day rule Anne is separately applying to two live cases, Mike Larson and Danny Peterson). Preauthorization (calling Concentra ahead of a visit) and close-call cost/frequency tracking (to build the safety-intervention case with BMs) discussed as build targets, not yet built. Also surfaced 9/3: a second, distinct late-reported injury (Sebastian Osuna, Houston) — unreported for ~a month, adjuster non-payment, a possible AFC/Workwell network gap — folded into this same overhaul. Trajectory: tracking yellow — real design commitments now exist with named owners (a step up from 8/26's strategy-only conversation), but the field reporting mechanism is still undecided and nothing is built yet against the 9/15 Green bar. 9/11 (post-wrap, live incident): a real WC injury came in and Anne personally ran the full sequence herself in ~15 minutes — submitted the pre-authorization, called Concentra to confirm the mover was pre-authorized, gave them the required information, and submitted the claim to Texas Mutual. goals.name: 100-Point Behavioral System — Q2 Rock 2 Companion
goals.assessment: 9/21 (group sync): the standing blocker RESOLVED — a damage alone is not a terminable offense, confirmed for both this system and the promotion framework. A single egregious act (Paul's example: slashing a couch) is gross misconduct, a separate category; sustained poor performance evidenced by damages can terminate. But three new problems opened against the same Oct 1 sign-off bar, which is why confidence drops 5→4 with nine days left and async review only (Cameron declined to schedule a working session). (1) DAMAGES MEASUREMENT IS CONTESTED: Mike wants damage-per-hour gone entirely in favour of a count or dollar threshold — his Dallas beta gives a point per damage regardless of value, and he says he'd need to fire five people immediately under it, with team members carrying 18+ damages. Anne and Cameron had designed around damages-per-hour across an hours/mileage gate. Paul disputes Mike's premise that reporting waits on resolution date, believes it runs off the estimate, and wants Matisen in a separate conversation to settle it. (2) SINGLE-BUCKET DILUTION: Mike's objection — aggregating everything lets someone be very bad in one dimension and hide it by being good elsewhere (in theory 25 callouts if a callout is 2 points against a 50-point threshold). Cameron agreed and named the inverse exposure: someone at three callouts could be one late arrival from termination, too shallow a pool. He asked Anne to map termination counts and the tiering question (third callout weighted heavier than the first two). (3) UNEMPLOYMENT ELIGIBILITY: Paul pushed twice that poor performance may not disqualify someone from unemployment the way attendance or misconduct does; Anne committed to research then Jennifer (attorney). Cameron's counter on the record: 'the cost of carrying a low performer costs more than the unemployment claim.' Anne's commitment: framework plus the mapped open questions to Brian, Mike and Paul by 9/24, async review, reconvene the following week. 9/17: Framework packaged and sent to Mike alongside his Dallas damage-accountability proposal — roadmap item 02 (stakeholder refine pass) moved from 'Cameron done, Mike/Brian pending' to Mike actively engaged with a concrete 5-question ask on damages, the biggest open dimension. Two design defects found and fixed on the HQ: (1) the thresholds card said 'rolling 6-month window' while majors expired at 12 months — contradictory, now defined by the heaviest deduction on file, with Anne's 12-month position recorded as open for Mike/Brian; (2) the roadmap promised a 'distribute 100 points across metrics' survey describing a category-multiplier the design doesn't have — cut, because severity values ARE the weighting. Survey scoped to branch managers only (movers cut). New finding, unresolved: the draft grid puts 4 damage-related redirects at 85 (termination review) vs. a warning at 4 in Mike's system — this framework is currently ~3x stricter on damages than the proposal it's being compared against. New open question logged: the Mover Promotion Framework gates damages/driving/attendance as separate bars while this system composites them, so the two can disagree about the same mover. 9/16: Green bar rewritten live in Anne/Cameron's 1:1 — the 'backtested against one real branch' clause is removed (the data's too dirty to trust a backtest) in favor of the methodology being fully mapped/weighted and signed off by Cameron and Paul by Oct 1; Super Green unchanged. 10 of 11 seeded open questions resolved 9/11 via a full stakeholder review with Cameron (one-pager + live call) plus Anne's own new /hr-consultants council (8 voices) and a targeted break round. Real mechanic changes landed: severe/terminable conduct now carries no points (immediate review gate instead); damages measured via redirect-pattern/aggregation, not single-incident dollar thresholds; score recovery redesigned — no praise buyback, a new separate Recognition Channel, rewards routed through bonus/promotion only; two-person review seat + first-six-months HR-held second seat made explicit; pilot widened from one branch to ~5, deliberately varied, since historical backtesting isn't reliable on current data; a new trailing-window visibility flag closes a pattern-gaming loophole. Framework is now heavily stress-tested by both an internal stakeholder pass and an independent HR-framework council — confidence up to 5. Full launch remains targeted Jan 1, 2027 per Cameron's 8/27 confirmation, not a Q3 deliverable; Q3's job (weighting-input survey) has not yet been built.
blockers: Damages measurement unresolved — Mike wants count/dollar-based (damage-per-hour 'needs to go away'), Anne and Cameron designed around damages-per-hour over an hours gate. Paul disputes Mike's premise about resolution-date lag and wants Matisen to settle the factual question.
Single-bucket dilution hole — Cameron asked Anne to map termination counts and whether tiering is needed (third callout weighted heavier than the first two) so the pool isn't too shallow.
Unemployment eligibility under a poor-performance termination — Paul's concern, unresolved. Anne researching, then Jennifer (attorney).
Framework + mapped open questions owed to Brian, Mike and Paul by 9/24. Async review only — Cameron declined a working session.
⚠️ Full launch still NOT a Q3 deliverable — targeted January 1, 2027 per Cameron's 8/27 confirmation.
goals.green: Methodology fully designed — every dimension (attendance, damages, CHOICES/professionalism, driver score) mapped to point values and weights, with an explicit rule for how damages get weighted based on attribution quality (not a flat weight) — signed off by Cameron and Paul by Oct 1.
goals.superGreen: Green + live scoring piloted on one full branch ahead of the Jan 1, 2027 company-wide launch, with 3 BMs trained to use the score in a real coaching conversation.

goals.name: Implement Bi-Weekly Start/Stop/Keep Conversations — Scaling Up Practice
goals.assessment: 9/21 (group sync): real movement — 'monumental movements across Friday, a little bit of Saturday, and today.' The app exists in draft with the repository and an HQ built; Anne walked the room through where it stands. Not published live yet — she flagged the cost and wants a walkthrough first. Working session LOCKED for Tuesday 9/22 afternoon with Mike, Brian and Amanda (Brian is in San Antonio Wednesday, so Tuesday was the only slot that held). Publish target: this week. Cameron restated the mechanic for the room — biweekly, ten minutes or less, someone at least two rungs below you, ideally in your own department to start, logged in the app. 45→55: the build and a booked session are genuine progress along the path, but adoption is what the bar measures and adoption is still zero, so this stays yellow. 9/21 CORRECTION to the same-day note below: the holdup IS in the record — it is in git, not on the board. Three real commits since Friday: the Replit deploy pipeline wired up (9/18), header branding + an expectation blurb added (9/18), and a live data fix today (9/21) falling back to department when an employee has no branch — that last one touched employees.json, ripplingSync.js and three front-end files, i.e. a roster-coverage bug found and fixed, not cosmetics. So this is a build-polish slip on an app being actively shipped, not a stall. Confidence holds at 4 and the earlier "cause not identified" read was wrong. 9/18: LAUNCH SLIPPED A SECOND TIME. The Friday 9/18 target did not hold; Anne's read on 9/21 is "in progress, will launch this week." This is the third target date (9/16 → 9/18 → week of 9/21). Percent held at 45 deliberately — the app has been data-complete since 9/10 and the Cameron finalisation meeting happened on 9/16, so the build is not the constraint, but nothing has been adopted and the bar is adoption. Against the REWRITTEN bar (all 7 leaders reporting two conversations through the tool before the Roundtable QGR) a mid-September week of slip is recoverable, which is why confidence holds at 4 rather than dropping. A third consecutive slip would make it a 3. Anne names this as the one thing she is personally moving this week. 9/16: Green bar rewritten live in Anne/Cameron's 1:1 — the Sept 15 date is removed (Super Green unchanged); the new bar is practice designed/documented and adopted by all 7 leaders, each reporting two Start/Stop/Keep conversations through the tool before the Roundtable QGR. ⚠️ 8/26 correction (Cameron + Anne): the goal was misread earlier the same day — what got built and shared with the other 6 Roundtable leaders' COS agents (a manager-to-own-direct-reports weekly checklist) was NOT the actual design; retracted same day. ✅ 8/27 (huddle + Cameron 1:1): mechanism fully redesigned and locked, then refined further per the cascading-chart edit Cameron made live in the 1:1 (surfaced via network digest 8/28, confirmed real by Anne). Every 2 weeks, each of the 7 Roundtable leaders calls someone **2+ rungs below them — never a direct report** — company-wide (deliberately cross-functional/cross-geography once comfortable; own-division fine at first) for a 5-minute start/stop/keep — no scheduling coordination, just find whoever's available. No manual assignment of who-talks-to-whom. Logged via a lightweight Replit submission app (not yet built) that tracks completion (who's done, who's missing) without adding admin work for the leaders. Immediate fires (safety, harassment) get triaged same-week; broader themes are digested quarterly — data collected through end of September, synthesized in October, folded into Q4 branch-level goals. Cameron explicitly said not to assume there will be themes — full adoption + honest tracking counts as success on its own, not a themes-found metric. Renamed Weekly → Bi-Weekly by Cameron 8/27 PM — report under this name going forward. 8/31 (Cameron sync): real open design gap surfaced — Anne is uneasy about the call-assignment mechanism (who calls whom, visibility across the 7 leaders so nobody double-covers or leaves gaps); Cameron floated narrowing by region/branch per leader, not yet resolved. **9/8: real forward motion.** Anne reviewed the full decision history on the rock pulse and sent Cameron a direct pushback: his own ratified Green-bar language says "random employee," which is the actual risk to his own adoption metric (cold calls from unscreened numbers don't get answered — it isn't scope creep, it's protecting the bar he already set), and flagged that no tracking log exists yet even though the bi-weekly cadence has already started. Also confirmed for the record (already discussed live, not an open question) that quarterly theme-aggregation over weekly was deliberate. Anne then kicked off the Replit submission-app build spec in a separate session (`start-stop-keep-app-build-spec-2026-09-08.md`) — first concrete step toward the app blocker. Trajectory: still yellow (no app live yet, adoption not started), but confidence up — this is the first session with real building motion instead of just design discussion, and Anne is actively pushing back on a bar-risk before it bites the metric instead of discovering it after adoption starts. **9/10: real technical unblock.** Paul's dedicated Rippling API token arrived and the app's first full company-wide sync ran live — 346 active employees, real manager/branch data, no longer the ~29-person manual branch-manager seed. In the process, caught and fixed a real correctness bug: the queue's leader/direct-report exclusion matched by name string, and Rippling's live display names don't reliably match how people are referred to elsewhere (e.g. "Mike Vandenbroader" vs Rippling's "Michael Vandenbroader") — this was silently letting leaders leak into each other's call queues and breaking direct-report exclusion for anyone with a mismatched manager name. Fixed to match by `ripplingId` first, falling back to name only when an ID is missing on one side. Also fixed a lookup bug that had left 28 of 346 people showing as "Unknown." Net effect: the submission-app blocker is substantially resolved — the app is data-complete and correctness-tested against real company data ahead of the planned 9/14 launch. What's left is the launch itself and adoption tracking, not the underlying build. Trajectory: confidence up to 5 — this is the first session where the app went from spec to working against real data, with a bug caught before launch rather than after. **9/14: launch missed — pushed to Friday 9/18, confidence back down to 4.** The 9/14 launch did not happen. The real holdup: Anne wants to meet with Cameron to finalize the app before flipping it on, and has been asking for that meeting since last week — it's now scheduled for Wednesday 9/16, two days after the original target. This is a dependency-on-Cameron delay, not a build or readiness problem on Anne's side. New target: Friday 9/18 (the official ratified Green-bar date is still Sept 15 per the 8/18 QGR table — that's now missed; whether the formal bar language itself moves is Cameron's call, not logged here yet).
blockers: Launch slipped twice (9/16 → 9/18 → week of 9/21) on deploy-pipeline and roster-data polish — actively being worked (3 commits 9/18–9/21). Nothing shipped yet, so adoption is still zero.

Rollout communication/marketing framing to employees not yet drafted — Cameron's own "random employee" Green-bar language still needs a pre-call heads-up mechanism or the adoption metric itself is at risk
